## The request this plan answers

> Review the repo and generate a step-by-step iterative work /plan with high /effort that encompasses exploratory analysis, spatial analysis, and statistical analysis. I want you to evaluate the data structure and distribution, identifying any caveats or limitations. Then recommend the most appropriate treatments or transformations of the vessel presence and apparent fishing effort data. I am most interested in analyzing cell x stage x gear and cell x month x gear relationships for the primary sets. For the spatial analysis, begin with Global Moran's I and Getis-Ord General G, then compare the efficacy of a Local Moran's I vs. Getis-Ord Gi* analysis. Following these tests, I want to assess the value of calculating and visualizing an autocorrelated kernel density estimate. I will gather turbine and cable location data with installation dates from Orsted, so we can also execute the BAG spatial-temporal models. Provide me with a comparison of approaches for a Tweedie GLMM, Hurdle model, or an Bayesian INLA-SPDE, including what conditions each of these approaches would require. I want the subsequent workflow to be written in R and grounded in FAIR data principles. Name the plan as gfw_analysis_plan.qmd in \planning. Include this prompt at the top of the document. If you have any questions, interview me.
:::

## Summary

The R workflow (`r/01`–`r/04`) ends with zero-filled cell tables for the
**Primary** and **Strict** sets. This plan covers everything after that, as
numbered qmds `r/05`–`r/14`. Each phase ends at a decision gate, and the
answer at each gate can change the next phase.

Six findings from profiling the current outputs (2026-10-06 pull, measured
2026-10-18) shape the design. Each is covered in @sec-structure and
@sec-caveats.

1. **The two datasets have different statistical shapes.** Vessel presence (VP)
   hours are effectively integer counts of *vessel × cell × day occupancy*:
   96.2% of Primary VP records are exactly 1 h. Apparent fishing effort (AFE)
   is continuous and non-negative with exact zeros. The monthly mean–variance
   power slope is about 1.2 for VP and about 1.7 for AFE. So VP calls for a
   **negative-binomial count model** and AFE for a **Tweedie or delta
   (hurdle) model**. One family for both would be wrong for one of them.
2. **Cell × month AFE is extremely sparse.** It is 97.7% zeros for mobile
   gear, 99.2% for fixed and 99.7% for pole-and-line. Of 3,376 cells, 1,941
   never have fixed-gear AFE and 2,775 never have pole-and-line AFE. Monthly
   AFE models need a domain defined from the baseline period and, for fixed
   gear, possibly a coarser time step.
3. **The stage means mix in different seasons.** Stage 2 (Oct 2020 – Mar 2023)
   holds three winters but only two summers. 33% of its months fall in the
   May–Sep window that carries 78% of fixed-gear AFE, against 44% in Stage 1
   and 46% in Stage 3. Raw stage-mean comparisons are biased against Stage 2
   unless they are standardised by season.
4. **A few vessels drive the effort signal.** The top 5 MMSIs carry 50% of
   Primary fixed-gear AFE, and one vessel carries 40% of pole-and-line AFE.
   PROVIDER (367717050) had June–September 2020 activity (1,452 AFE h) that
   looked like its charter work: 66% of hours inside the leases, against 23.3%
   for the rest of the Stage 1 fleet. Its charter window now starts on
   **2020-06-18**, the first day of that in-lease activity. That cuts Stage 1
   mobile AFE by 16% (caveat 11 in @sec-caveats).
5. **Global autocorrelation is strong in every surface.** Moran's I runs from
   0.20 to 0.77 and every z exceeds 23. The global tests will therefore confirm
   clustering rather than discover it. Their value is in comparing effect sizes
   across gear and stage, and in setting the spatial scale for the later
   models.
6. **The BAG gradient is short and has no far-field control.** Every cell lies
   within about 15 km of a lease. 893 cells (26%) are inside one, and only 130
   are more than 10 km away. With the within-AOI design chosen in the
   interview, BAG supports inference about **redistribution relative to the
   outer ring**, not about net change in regional effort.

## Data structure and distribution {#sec-structure}

All figures are for the **Primary set** unless labelled otherwise. They were
measured on 2026-10-18 from the 2026-10-06 pull, after PROVIDER's window
moved to 2020-06-18 and 03 and 04 were re-run. `06_explore.qmd` recomputes
every one of them at render time, so these typed values are a record of what
justified the design, not values to quote.

### Grid and support

- **3,376 cells**: 3,118 `inside`, 206 `edge`, 52 `outside`.
- `area_km2` ranges from 0.929 to 0.937. The 0.9% range means the area offset
  barely changes the results, but keep it so results are in density units
  (h km⁻² month⁻¹) and stay comparable with other grids.
- Queen contiguity, rebuilt from the `ix`/`iy` lattice, gives a mean of 7.80
  neighbours, one connected component and no islands. 02's `poly2nb()` on the
  corner-built grid should give the same weights. Phase 0 asserts that they
  match.

### Composition of the Primary set

| | VP | AFE |
|---|---:|---:|
| Records | 93,295 | 20,241 |
| MMSIs | 1,381 | 414 |
| MOBILE MMSIs / hours | 771 / 66,599 | 277 / 23,374 |
| FIXED MMSIs / hours | 138 / 21,842 | 61 / 5,215 |
| POLE_AND_LINE MMSIs / hours | 473 / 9,976 | 76 / 2,023 |
| UNRESOLVED hours | **0** | **0** |

Every Primary record has a resolved gear class, so the `UNRESOLVED` rows in the
Primary gear tables are structural zeros. Drop them in Phase 0. In Strict,
`UNRESOLVED` carries 58,078 AFE hours in Stage 3, so a gear-specific Strict
analysis is not interpretable. Strict is used only for all-gear comparisons.

### Record-level distributions

- **VP hours per record** are integers from 1 to 15. 96.2% are exactly 1 h,
  2.9% are 2 h and 0.3% are more than 3 h. A cell-month VP total is therefore
  close to a count of **vessel-days with at least one AIS position in the
  cell**. It measures occupancy and is dominated by transits.
- **AFE hours per record**: median 1.00, 90th percentile 2.86, 99th percentile
  11.1, maximum 24.3. 64 records are exactly 0 h and 1,708 are below 0.32 h.
  The archived Python pipeline dropped records at or below 0.32 h; the R
  pipeline keeps them. Keep them, and add a sensitivity run that drops them.

### Cell × stage × gear

| Gear | VP % zero (S1/S2/S3) | VP var/mean | AFE % zero (S1/S2/S3) | AFE var/mean |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| MOBILE | 8.9 / 22.9 / 8.4 | 10.7–15.5 | 52.2 / 72.4 / 39.6 | 11–22 |
| FIXED | 36.8 / 33.9 / 15.0 | 2.7–5.8 | 86.2 / 87.8 / 71.9 | 7.6–10.6 |
| POLE_AND_LINE | 61.2 / 65.6 / 40.8 | 6.8–26 | 95.2 / 93.8 / 89.0 | 10–57 |

- Every cell is overdispersed (variance/mean well above 1), so Poisson does not
  fit.
- Stage 2 has more zeros than both neighbours for VP mobile and AFE mobile and
  fixed. The gap is widest for mobile AFE: 72.4% zero in Stage 2, against
  52.2% in Stage 1 and 39.6% in Stage 3, with all of PROVIDER's charter hours
  excluded. The
  pattern fits the seasonal-composition confound in caveat 8 in @sec-caveats,
  before any project effect is considered.
- A typical occupied cell has 1–4 MMSIs. For fixed and pole-and-line gear, a
  third to a half of occupied cells hold one vessel only.

### Cell × month × gear

| Gear | VP % zero | AFE % zero | VP cells never active | AFE cells never active | VP median active months (of 128) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| MOBILE | 89.3 | 97.7 | 47 | 657 | 8 |
| FIXED | 95.6 | 99.2 | 128 | 1,941 | 4.5 |
| POLE_AND_LINE | 98.2 | 99.7 | 735 | 2,775 | 2 |

**Mean–variance power** (slope of log variance on log mean across cells, monthly):

| | MOBILE | FIXED | POLE_AND_LINE |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| VP | 1.18 | 1.12 | 1.24 |
| AFE | 1.67 | 1.67 | 1.71 |

This is a first estimate of the Tweedie power *p*. For VP, *p* ≈ 1.2 is close
to the Poisson boundary, which supports a count family. For AFE, *p* ≈ 1.7
sits well inside the compound Poisson–gamma range (1 < *p* < 2).

**Seasonality.** Share of hours by month-of-year:

- Fixed-gear AFE: 78% falls in May–Sep.
- Mobile VP: 40% falls in Jun–Aug.
- Pole-and-line VP: 47% falls in Jul–Aug.

Every monthly model needs a cyclic month-of-year term.

**Trend in AIS coverage.** Distinct Primary MMSIs per year rose from 354
(2016) to 603 (2025) for VP, and from 63 to 129 for AFE. Fixed-gear VP rose
from 25 to 280 occupied cells per month. Part of that rise is AIS uptake, not
effort (@sec-cav-ais).

## Caveats and limitations {#sec-caveats}

Each caveat comes with the treatment this plan applies to it. Report them in
the methods with numbers recomputed at render time, not typed.

### Measurement

1. **VP hours count occupancy, not duration.** VP is the number of hours with
   at least one position, so a vessel crossing a cell scores 1 h whether it
   stays 5 minutes or 59. *Treatment:* model VP as a count and describe it as
   "vessel-day occupancy" in the text. Do not add VP and AFE hours together.
2. **AFE is a model output, not observed fishing.** GFW's fishing classifier is
   most accurate for trawlers, longliners and purse seiners. It is less
   validated for pots, traps and gillnets, whose AIS tracks look like slow
   transits. *Treatment:* state it. Treat fixed-gear AFE as the least reliable
   surface, and have VP replicate every fixed-gear finding.
3. **AFE is near zero, by construction, for the 142 hulls Primary adds.** GFW
   computes effort only for vessels it types as fishing. *Treatment:* the
   sensitivity run uses the imputation already in `04` (@sec-sensitivity).
4. **Sub-threshold AFE.** 1,808 Primary AFE records are below 0.32 h and 64 are
   exactly 0. *Treatment:* keep them, and add a sensitivity run that drops them.

### Coverage and representativeness {#sec-cav-ais}

5. **AIS carriage is uneven by gear and changes over time.** The 2016 USCG rule
   requires AIS on commercial fishing vessels of 65 ft and over. Most SNE
   pot and gillnet boats are smaller and carry AIS voluntarily, so fixed gear
   and pole-and-line are **undercounted, and the undercount shrinks over
   time**. The 10× rise in occupied fixed-gear VP cells from 2016 to 2025
   is partly uptake.
   *Treatment:*
   - In the BAG design, an AOI-wide uptake trend cancels out of the gradient
     contrast, but only if uptake is **spatially uniform** across the distance
     bands. Check that assumption (Phase 1, step 7).
   - Add a fleet-size covariate (active MMSIs per gear per month, AOI-wide) as
     a sensitivity term.
   - Never interpret a rise in AOI-total effort as more fishing.
6. **No external control.** With the within-AOI design (interview decision), an
   AOI-wide change cannot be separated from regional trends, the 2020 COVID
   market disruption or AIS uptake. *Treatment:* claims are limited to spatial
   redistribution relative to the 8–15 km ring (@sec-bag-limits).
7. **Possible AIS switch-off.** Vessels can stop transmitting near construction
   for security or competitive reasons. That would look like avoidance.
   *Treatment:* state it as an alternative explanation. If an MMSI
   disappears inside the leases during construction but stays active
   elsewhere, its gaps can be checked in the record-level data.

### Design

8. **Season composition differs between stages**. Stage 2 is
   33% May–Sep months; Stages 1 and 3 are 44% and 46%. *Treatment:* report
   **season-standardised stage rates** (the mean of the 12 month-of-year means
   within each stage) next to the raw stage rates. The monthly models absorb
   season with a cyclic term. Expect part of the "Stage 2 dip" to disappear
   after standardisation.
9. **Stage lengths differ** (57 / 30 / 41 months). *Treatment:* use rates (hours
   ÷ months) in descriptives and an offset of `log(months × area_km2)` in the
   models.
10. **One window holds very different disturbances.** Stage 3 combines seabed
    preparation, construction and operation at three projects on different
    schedules. The interview kept the three stages. *Treatment:* the monthly
    BAG uses the Ørsted dates to give each cell its own exposure timing.
11. **PROVIDER's Stage 1 activity in 2020 looked like charter work.** With
    its window starting on 2020-10-01, it kept 1,452 AFE h and 1,651 VP h
    before that date, almost all from June to September 2020 (it has 1 AFE h
    in total before 2020).
    - Those months put 66% of its AFE hours inside the leases (36% in June
      rising to 80% in September) at 17 h per active day.
    - Its confirmed charter period is 55–64% in the leases at 16–19 h per day.
    - The rest of the Stage 1 fleet is 23.3% (AFE) and 16.1% (VP) inside the
      leases, so PROVIDER's pre-window share was about three times the
      fleet's. (Measured with PROVIDER's own pre-window hours in the fleet,
      the shares were 28.9% / 18.3%.)

    A screen of every charter hull's last 12 months before its window
    finds no other case: the next highest is Ashley Ann (338328681) at 20%
    (AFE). PROVIDER made up 1,452 of the 2,878 h (50%) of Primary mobile AFE
    in June–September 2020.

    **Decision (2026-10-18):** `valid_from` moved from 2020-10-01 to
    **2020-06-18** in `references/vessel_decisions.csv`.

    *Reasoning:*
    - 2020-06-18 is the first day with in-lease hours in both VP and AFE.
      From then the pattern runs unbroken, at 16–20 h per day, into the
      confirmed window.
    - Before 2020 the hull has no fishing baseline to depart from: 1 AFE h
      (2018) and scattered 1–4 h VP days in the summers of 2017–2019.
    - The in-lease share and daily intensity match its confirmed charter
      period, not the fleet's.
    - It is the only charter hull with this pattern.

    One day before the window, 2020-06-09 (4 AFE h, outside the leases),
    stays as fishing, as do all earlier records. The window starts before
    Stage 2 (2020-10-01), so this row is a dated exclusion inside Stage 1. It
    does not follow the `stages_2_3` convention of the removal list.

    *Effect, measured after the re-run of 03 and 04 (2026-10-18):*

    | Primary, mobile gear | Before | After |
    |---|---:|---:|
    | Stage 1 AFE hours | 9,213 | 7,765 (−16%) |
    | Stage 1 AFE zero cells | 43.2% | 52.2% |
    | Stage 1 VP hours | 27,826 | 26,207 (−6%) |
    | Jun–Sep 2020 AFE hours | 2,878 | 1,430 |
    | Stage 1 AFE Moran's I | 0.44 | 0.42 |

    PROVIDER's only Primary AFE record is now 2020-06-09.

    *Treatment:*
    - Make the pre-window screen a standing check in `06` (Phase 1, step 5),
      so every charter window is tested against the activity just before it.
    - Phase 8 keeps the "exclude 2020" run, for COVID and the stage boundary.

### Statistical

12. **Effort is concentrated in few vessels.** For fixed AFE the top 5 vessels
    carry 50% and the top 10 carry 72%. For pole-and-line AFE one vessel
    carries 40%. A cell's value often comes from a single hull. *Treatment:*
    - Run a leave-one-vessel-out jackknife over the top 10 MMSIs per gear on
      every headline result.
    - As an optional extension, fit a vessel-level model with an MMSI random
      effect (@sec-models-vessel).
    - Report n_MMSI next to every map.
13. **Exact zeros: structural or sampling?** A zero in a cell that a gear never
    uses (wrong depth or substrate, a closure) is structural. A zero in a
    fished cell in a quiet month is sampling. *Treatment:* define each gear's
    model domain from **Stage 1 activity**, never from the whole series. A
    domain chosen from all stages would drop cells abandoned because of the
    projects, which conditions on the outcome.
14. **Autocorrelation in space and time.** Spatial autocorrelation is strong in
    every surface, and each cell is measured repeatedly over months.
    *Treatment:* every model carries a spatial random field or smooth plus a
    temporal term, and the residuals are tested for leftover autocorrelation.
15. **Multiple testing in the local statistics.** There are 3,376 tests per
    surface, across 2 datasets × 3 gears × 3 stages. *Treatment:*
    Benjamini–Hochberg FDR within each surface, with seeded conditional
    permutation.
16. **Gi\* cannot find cold spots at a floor of zero.** On AFE surfaces with
    40–95% zeros, a cell cannot sit significantly below a mean that is itself
    near zero. The archive already recorded this. *Treatment:* report it as a
    property of the statistic, not a finding (@sec-local).

## Recommended treatments and transformations {#sec-treatments}

One principle runs through this section: **transform for descriptive spatial
statistics, never for the models.** The models fit raw hours with an
appropriate family and an exposure offset.

### Derived quantities (Phase 0)

| Field | Definition | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `rate` | hours ÷ months in the time step | Comparing stages |
| `density` | hours ÷ (months × `area_km2`) | Maps, descriptives (h km⁻² month⁻¹) |
| `log_expo` | `log(months × area_km2)` | Model offset |
| `y_vst` | Variance-stabilised density (below) | Moran's I, General G, LISA, Gi\* |
| `dist_lease_km` | Signed distance from cell centroid to the nearest lease boundary (negative inside) | BAG gradient |
| `dist_band` | `inside`, `0–2`, `2–4`, `4–8`, `8–15` km | BAG factor. At least 280 cells per band; 8–15 is the reference. |
| `nearest_project` | SFW / RWF / SRW | Project-specific gradients |
| `x_km`, `y_km` | Centroid in EPSG:32619, km | Spatial fields and the mesh |
| `moy`, `year`, `t_index` | Month of year, year, month index | Seasonality and trend |
| `domain_{gear}` | Cell active for that gear in Stage 1 (VP or AFE > 0) | Model domain (@sec-caveats, item 13) |
| `depth_m`, `slope_deg`, `depth_sd_m`, `bpi_broad` | Per-cell bathymetry and terrain summaries | Static environmental covariates (@sec-env) |
| `habitat_*` | Per-cell habitat class shares, once the Ørsted data arrive | Static environmental covariates (@sec-env) |

### Environmental covariates: bathymetry and benthic habitat {#sec-env}

Depth and seabed type set *where* each gear fishes. Trawlers work soft
sediment at particular depths; pots and gillnets work hard bottom and edges.
Adding them to the models does three things:

- it explains part of the baseline spatial pattern;
- it makes the stationary SPDE field more plausible, since the field no longer
  has to absorb depth gradients;
- it sharpens the BAG contrast, by comparing cells of similar habitat at
  different distances from the turbines.

Both covariates are **static**. They cannot confound the period × distance
(BAG) interaction, which varies over time. They can be collinear with the
distance *main effect*, and with the spatial field (spatial confounding).
Phase 6 checks both (below).

#### Bathymetry: NCEI Coastal Relief Model Vol. 1 (2023)

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Source | NOAA NCEI U.S. Coastal Relief Model, Volume 1 (Northeast Atlantic), 2023 release, 1 arc-second (≈ 30 m), built from NCEI's CUDEM tiles. File `crm_vol1_2023.nc` (≈ 1.6 GB for the whole volume) in the THREDDS catalog `https://www.ngdc.noaa.gov/thredds/catalog/crm/cudem/catalog.html` |
| Request | **Only the AOI bounding box plus a 5 km buffer**, via THREDDS (NetCDF Subset or OPeNDAP) or NCEI's grid-extract tool. Never the full volume. Record the exact request URL, access date and returned file hash in the provenance sidecar. |
| Vertical datum | EGM2008 (≈ mean sea level), metres, negative down. Convert to positive `depth_m` and record the datum. |
| Storage | `data/sf/bathy/crm_vol1_2023_aoi.tif` (GeoTIFF, EPSG:4326 as delivered), with a `.json` provenance sidecar. Written by `05`; nothing is edited by hand. |
| Licence | US Government work, public domain. Cite the DOI given on NCEI's record. |
| Fallback | GEBCO 2024 (15 arc-second) if CRM access fails. It is coarser than the 0.84 × 1.11 km cells but enough for mean depth. |

**Derived per-cell covariates** (in `05`, with `terra`):

1. Project the raster to EPSG:32619 with bilinear resampling (30 m).
2. Derive terrain layers at 30 m:
   - slope (`terra::terrain(v = "slope")`);
   - a **broad-scale bathymetric position index**: depth minus the focal mean
     in a 1–3 km annulus (`terra::focal`). It separates ridges and banks from
     troughs at the scale of the grid.
3. Summarise each layer to the grid cells with area-weighted extraction
   (`terra::extract(..., exact = TRUE)`): mean depth, SD of depth (a rugosity
   proxy), mean slope and mean BPI.
4. Checks:
   - every cell has a non-missing depth;
   - all depths are positive (the AOI does not touch land);
   - the range matches the CRM for the region;
   - a map of `depth_m` sits alongside the effort maps in `06`.

**Treatment in the models:**

- Centre and scale each covariate.
- Enter depth as a low-rank smooth (`s(depth_m, k = 4)`, or a quadratic in
  INLA), because gear-depth responses peak at intermediate depths.
- Enter slope / BPI linearly.
- Check collinearity with `dist_lease_km`: Spearman ρ, concurvity for
  `mgcv`-type smooths, VIF for linear terms.
- If |ρ| > 0.7, keep depth in the model and report that the distance *main*
  effect is not separately identified. The BAG interaction still is.

#### Benthic habitat: Ørsted classification (pending)

Ask Ørsted for the layer in this form, and log the request in the open items:

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `geometry` | POLYGON, or a raster of classes | With its CRS |
| `habitat_class` | string | Ideally CMECS substrate classes (group / subgroup) as used in BOEM site characterisation, or Ørsted's own scheme with a crosswalk to CMECS |
| `survey`, `survey_date`, `method` | string / date | E.g. MBES + backscatter + grab / video ground truth |
| `confidence` | string / numeric | Classification confidence where available |
| *Coverage polygon* | POLYGON | **Essential**: the area actually surveyed |

**Coverage is the main risk.** Site-characterisation surveys usually cover the
lease areas and cable corridors, not the 10 km buffer. A covariate that exists
only inside the leases is perfectly confounded with being inside a lease, so
it cannot enter the full-AOI models. The rules:

1. **Covers ≥ 95% of the AOI:** add per-cell habitat shares (`habitat_*`,
   compositional; drop one reference class) as fixed effects in every model.
2. **Covers the leases and corridors only:**
   - use it *inside* the leases, to stratify the lease-level results (e.g.
     fixed-gear effort on hard vs soft bottom inside the arrays);
   - for the full-AOI models, use a regional substrate product with full
     coverage instead (USGS usSEABED sediment, or the sediment layers on the
     Northeast Ocean Data Portal);
   - run the Ørsted layer as a sensitivity on the covered cells.
3. Either way, record the class scheme and crosswalk in
   `references/data_dictionary.md`. Store the layer under `data/sf/habitat/`
   with the sharing terms noted in `references/`.

### Variance-stabilising transforms for the spatial statistics

The Tweedie variance function Var(Y) ∝ μ^*p* is stabilised by
Y^(1 − *p*/2). Using the measured powers:

| Dataset | *p* | Stabilising exponent | Recommended |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| VP | ≈ 1.2 | ≈ 0.4 | **√ density** (Anscombe-like for counts). Matches the archived analysis, so the results stay comparable. |
| AFE | ≈ 1.7 | ≈ 0.15 | **log(density + *c*)**, with *c* = half the smallest positive density in that surface |

- Avoid `log1p(density)`. Densities are around 0.01–1 h km⁻² month⁻¹, and
  `log1p` of values that small is close to the identity, so it stabilises
  nothing. A log with a stated, data-derived constant is reproducible and
  scale-aware.
- Moran's I and Gi\* are invariant to multiplying the whole surface by a
  constant. Within one stage, √(hours) and √(density) give the same statistic,
  but log does not, which is why *c* is defined per surface.
- Sensitivity: raw density and the alternative transform (√ for AFE, log for
  VP) for every global and local statistic.

### Response families for the models

| Response | Family | Why |
|---|---|---|
| VP, cell × stage | **Negative binomial (NB2)**, log link | Integer, overdispersed (var/mean 3–26), few zeros for mobile |
| VP, cell × month | **NB2**. Hurdle-NB if DHARMa flags excess zeros (likely for fixed and pole-and-line). | 89–98% zeros. NB alone may fit mobile. |
| AFE, cell × stage | **Tweedie** (*p* estimated) *vs* **delta-Gamma** | Continuous with exact zeros. *p* ≈ 1.7. |
| AFE, cell × month | **Delta-Gamma / delta-lognormal** (hurdle) | 97–99.7% zeros. Occupancy and intensity probably respond differently near turbines (@sec-models). |

### Scope per gear

| Gear | VP stage | VP month | AFE stage | AFE month |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| MOBILE | Full | Full | Full | Full |
| FIXED | Full | Full | Full | Domain-restricted; season × year time step if the monthly fit fails |
| POLE_AND_LINE | Full | Full | Descriptive + global statistics only | **Not modelled.** Only 601 cells were ever positive, and one vessel holds 40% of the hours. |

Each gear is modelled **separately**. A joint gear-interaction model is fitted
only to test formally whether the BAG effect differs between mobile and fixed
gear (@sec-models).

## Workflow overview {#sec-workflow}

New qmds continue the numbered `r/` sequence and the conventions already in
place:

- Every path goes in `r/paths.R`, with a Quarto-parameter override.
- Shared code lives in a sourced helper file with `testthat` tests.
- The setup chunk finds the repo root.
- Each qmd ends with `sessionInfo()` and `renv::diagnostics()`.
- No absolute paths, and no typed statistics in prose.

| Step | File | Phase | Writes (gitignored) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 05 | `05_prepare_analysis.qmd` | 0: analysis tables, covariates, weights | `data/processed/analysis/` |
| 06 | `06_explore.qmd` | 1: EDA | figures, tables |
| 07 | `07_spatial_global.qmd` | 2: Global Moran's I, General G, correlograms | `spatial/global_*.csv` |
| 08 | `08_spatial_local.qmd` | 3: Local Moran's I vs Gi\*, change classes | `spatial/local_*.gpkg` |
| 09 | `09_infrastructure.qmd` | 4: Ørsted turbines and cables → time-varying covariates | `data/sf/infra/`, covariate tables |
| 10 | `10_bag.qmd` | 5: BAG models | `models/bag_*.rds` |
| 11 | `11_models_frequentist.qmd` | 6: Tweedie and hurdle GLMMs (`glmmTMB`, `sdmTMB`) | `models/freq_*.rds` |
| 12 | `12_models_inla.qmd` | 7: INLA-SPDE | `models/inla_*.rds` |
| 13 | `13_sensitivity.qmd` | 8: sensitivity grid | `sensitivity/*.csv` |
| 14 | `14_synthesis.qmd` | 9: results and figures for the thesis | `reports/figures/` |

Shared code: `r/analysis_helpers.R` (derived fields, weights, transforms,
domain flags, the model cache) and `r/spatial_helpers.R` (wrappers for
global and local statistics, change classes). Each gets a test file in
`r/tests/testthat/`.

**Runtime and caching.** R renders are not frozen (see `r/_quarto.yml`), and
the INLA and spatiotemporal models can take hours. The helper
`fit_cached(key_inputs, fit_fun)` hashes the model formula, the input table and
the package versions with `digest` (already in `renv.lock`). It saves the fit
to `data/processed/models/<hash>.rds` with a JSON metadata sidecar, and re-fits
only when the hash changes. This avoids adding `targets` as a dependency. If
the pipeline grows past this, `targets` is the next step.

**New dependencies.** Approved on 2026-10-18 to add phase by phase. Install
each one when its phase starts and record it with `renv::snapshot()` in the
same commit as the code that first uses it.

| Package | Phase | Source | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spdep` | 2–3 | already in renv | Weights, Moran's I, General G, `localmoran_perm`, `localG_perm` |
| `terra` | 0 | CRAN | Bathymetry subset, reprojection, terrain derivatives, area-weighted extraction (@sec-env) |
| `mgcv` | 5–6 | **pinned 2026-10-18** (1.9-3) | Cyclic smooths, the GAM alternative |
| `glmmTMB` | 5–6 | CRAN | Tweedie, NB2 and hurdle GLMMs |
| `DHARMa` | 5–7 | CRAN | Simulation-based residual diagnostics |
| `sdmTMB` | 6 | CRAN | SPDE random fields with Tweedie and delta families, spatial-block CV |
| `fmesher` | 6–7 | CRAN | SPDE meshes, shared by `sdmTMB` and `INLA` |
| `marginaleffects` | 5–6 | CRAN | Marginal predictions and contrasts from the two hurdle parts |
| `INLA` | 7 | **not on CRAN**: `https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable` | Bayesian SPDE |
| `inlabru` | 7 (optional) | CRAN | Simpler syntax for joint hurdle likelihoods |

## Phase 0: Analysis tables, covariates and weights (`05_prepare_analysis.qmd`) {#sec-phase0}

**Goal.** A tidy, documented analysis table per dataset × time step, keyed on
`cell_id`, with every derived field from @sec-treatments and saved weights.

**Steps**

1. Read the four gear tables. Filter to `set == "primary"` and drop the
   `UNRESOLVED` rows, after asserting they sum to 0 h. Keep Strict in a
   separate object for `13`.
2. Join the grid attributes (`area_km2`, `aoi_class`, centroid `x_km`/`y_km`)
   and the stage lengths from `dev_stages`.
3. Compute the derived fields: `rate`, `density`, `log_expo`, `y_vst`, `moy`,
   `year`, `t_index`.
4. Compute lease distances. Reproject the three leases to 32619, then derive
   the signed distance, `dist_band` and `nearest_project`.
5. Compute the domain flags `domain_{gear}` from Stage 1 only.
6. Bathymetry (@sec-env):
   - fetch the AOI subset of `crm_vol1_2023.nc`, with a hash check and
     provenance sidecar; skip the fetch if the stored file's hash matches;
   - derive slope and BPI;
   - extract the per-cell summaries and join them to `cells.gpkg`.

   Habitat shares are added in the same step once the Ørsted layer arrives.
7. Weights:
   - Rebuild queen contiguity both ways (02's `poly2nb()` and the lattice from
     `ix`/`iy`) and assert they are identical.
   - Assert 1 component, no islands and a mean above 7.7.
   - Write the neighbour list as a GAL file (`spdep::write.nb.gal`), which is
     interoperable with GeoDa and PySAL.
   - Build two weights objects: `lw_W` (row-standardised, for Moran's I and
     LISA) and `lw_B_self` (binary, self-inclusive, for General G and Gi\*).
8. Write `data/processed/analysis/{vp,afe}_{stage,month}_gear.csv` and
   `cells.gpkg` (geometry plus static covariates, including bathymetry), each with a JSON
   provenance sidecar (@sec-fair).

```{r}
#| label: phase0-weights
library(spdep)

lattice_nb <- function(ix, iy, ids) {
  key <- setNames(seq_along(ix), paste(ix, iy))
  nb <- lapply(seq_along(ix), function(i) {
    cand <- paste(ix[i] + rep(-1:1, 3), iy[i] + rep(-1:1, each = 3))
    j <- unname(key[cand])
    sort(as.integer(j[!is.na(j) & j != i]))
  })
  structure(nb, class = "nb", region.id = ids, type = "queen", sym = TRUE)
}

nb_poly    <- poly2nb(grid, queen = TRUE, snap = 0)
nb_lattice <- lattice_nb(grid$ix, grid$iy, grid$cell_id)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(nb_poly, nb_lattice, check.attributes = FALSE)),
          n.comp.nb(nb_poly)$nc == 1, all(card(nb_poly) > 0),
          mean(card(nb_poly)) > 7.7)

lw_W      <- nb2listw(nb_poly, style = "W")                # Moran's I, LISA
lw_B_self <- nb2listw(include.self(nb_poly), style = "B")  # General G, Gi*
write.nb.gal(nb_poly, file.path(paths$analysis, "grid_queen.gal"))
```

**Gate.** All assertions pass. Hours in the analysis table equal hours in the
interim table, per gear × time step.

## Phase 1: Exploratory analysis (`06_explore.qmd`) {#sec-phase1}

**Goal.** Recompute everything in @sec-structure at render time, and test the
assumptions the later phases rest on.

**Steps**

1. **Composition.** Hours, records and MMSIs by gear × stage × dataset, raw
   and season-standardised (caveat 8).
2. **Distribution diagnostics** per dataset × gear × stage and per month:
   - percent zero, mean, variance, var/mean, skewness;
   - quantiles of the positive values;
   - Tweedie power by the log-variance/log-mean slope, and by profile
     likelihood (`glmmTMB` fits with *p* free, once installed);
   - for VP, check that `vp_hours` is integer.
3. **Transform check.** Skew and the mean–variance slope of `y_vst` against
   raw density, √ and log for each surface. This confirms or overrides the
   choices in @sec-treatments.
4. **Time series.** Monthly Primary VP and AFE by gear, split inside/outside
   the leases and by `dist_band`, with the stage boundaries marked. Include
   STL or cyclic-smooth decompositions of trend and season.
5. **Vessel concentration and the pre-window screen.**
   - Lorenz curves and top-*k* shares per gear × stage.
   - Profile any vessel holding more than 10% of a gear × stage total.
   - For every hull with a charter or survey window, compare the share of its
     hours inside the leases in the 12 months before the window with the
     fleet's share. Flag hulls more than twice the fleet share. PROVIDER is
     the current case (caveat 11).
6. **Depth and effort.** Effort density against `depth_m` and BPI per gear.
   Check the expected gear–depth niches, and the collinearity of depth with
   `dist_lease_km`.
7. **Is AIS uptake spatially uniform?** (The key BAG assumption.) Plot the
   trend in active MMSIs per `dist_band` per gear, and in the all-vessel raw VP
   per band (`gfw_vp_id_cell_month.csv`). Do the bands rise in parallel
   *before* construction (Stages 1–2)? Test with a `band × year` interaction
   restricted to Stages 1–2.
8. **Maps.** Density maps per gear × stage on one shared colour scale, with the
   lease outlines and the n_MMSI per cell. Reuse the committed basemap rasters
   in `references/basemap/`.
9. **Temporal completeness** per cell × gear (active months / 128). This
   decides which surfaces can carry a monthly model.

**Gate.**

- Step 7 shows parallel pre-construction trends across bands → proceed with the
  within-AOI BAG.
- If not, add a `band × year` pre-trend term to every BAG model and say so.
- Any hull flagged in step 5 goes back to `03` for a decision before the
  Stage 1 baseline is used for inference. PROVIDER was the first case and was
  resolved on 2026-10-18 (caveat 11).

## Phase 2: Global spatial autocorrelation (`07_spatial_global.qmd`) {#sec-global}

**Goal.** Measure how much each surface clusters, how that changes across
stages and months, and the spatial scale of the clustering. The scale feeds the
Phase 3 weights and the SPDE range priors.

**Statistics**

| Statistic | Weights | Detects | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Moran's I** | `lw_W` | Similar values together, high or low | `moran.mc(nsim = 999)`, seeded. Report I with a permutation 95% interval, not just p. |
| **Getis-Ord General G** | binary (`style = "B"`), no self | Whether *high* values cluster more than low ones | Needs non-negative values, which holds. `globalG.test()`. Read with Moran's I: a high I with an unremarkable G means the low values drive the clustering. |
| *(optional)* Geary's C | `lw_W` | Local differences | A cross-check on Moran's I |

**Steps**

1. Moran's I and General G on `y_vst` for each dataset × gear × stage
   (18 surfaces), plus the raw-density sensitivity.
2. Moran's I **per month** for each gear. Plot I(t) with the stage boundaries
   and a seasonal smooth. Is clustering itself changing as construction goes
   on?
3. **Correlograms.** Moran's I by contiguity order 1–10 (`sp.correlogram`)
   and by distance band (0–2, 2–4, … 20 km). The distance where I falls to
   about 0.1 gives:
   - the candidate neighbourhood for the Phase 3 weight sensitivity;
   - an empirical prior for the Matérn range in Phase 7 (*ρ*₀).
4. Summary figure: I and G z by gear × stage, with the season-standardised
   version alongside.

```{r}
#| label: phase2-global
set.seed(42)
global_stats <- function(y, lw_W, lw_B) {
  mi <- moran.mc(y, lw_W, nsim = 999, return_boot = TRUE)
  gg <- globalG.test(y, lw_B)
  tibble(I = mi$statistic, I_lo = quantile(mi$res, .025), I_hi = quantile(mi$res, .975),
         I_p = mi$p.value, G = gg$estimate[1], G_z = gg$statistic, G_p = gg$p.value)
}
lw_B <- nb2listw(nb_poly, style = "B")   # General G: binary, no self
```

(`mi$res` is the permutation reference distribution under the null. The
interval for I itself comes from a cell-block bootstrap, which is cheap.)

**Gate.**

- Correlogram range below about 3 km → queen weights are adequate.
- Range above about 5 km → add a distance-band weights run to Phase 3.
- Write *ρ*₀ to the provenance sidecar for Phase 7.

## Phase 3: Local Moran's I vs Getis-Ord Gi\* (`08_spatial_local.qmd`) {#sec-local}

**Goal.** Compare the two local statistics on these data using pre-specified
criteria, then adopt one as the primary hotspot method, with the other in a
defined supporting role.

### What each statistic answers

| | Local Moran's I (LISA) | Getis-Ord Gi\* |
|---|---|---|
| Question | Is this cell similar to, or different from, its neighbours? | Is the neighbourhood sum, including the cell, unusually high or low? |
| Output | HH, LL, HL, LH clusters and outliers | Hot / cold, z-score |
| Weights | Row-standardised (`lw_W`) | Binary, self-inclusive (`lw_B_self`). The archive found that row-standardised Gi\* gives zero hotspots. |
| Inference | Conditional permutation (`localmoran_perm`) | Analytic z, or permutation (`localG_perm`). On skewed data the analytic normal approximation is poor, so **use permutation.** |
| Weak point here | LL in empty sea means nothing, and outliers are unstable in sparse surfaces | No cold spots at a floor of zero (caveat 16), and no outlier class |

### Comparison criteria

All criteria are fixed before the results are seen.

1. **Agreement.** Cohen's κ between Gi\* hot and LISA HH (and between cold and
   LL) per surface, with maps of the cells where they disagree.
2. **Behaviour on zero-inflated surfaces.** The share of significant LL / cold
   cells that are all-zero neighbourhoods. A statistic that labels empty sea
   "significant" is not informative about effort.
3. **Unique information.** How many HL / LH outliers there are and where:
   - inside the leases (isolated high fixed-gear cells next to turbines);
   - on lease boundaries.
   Gi\* cannot give this.
4. **Stability.** For each statistic, the share of runs in which a cell keeps
   its significant class across:
   - the leave-one-vessel-out jackknife (top 10 MMSIs per gear, re-aggregated
     from the record-level file);
   - permutation seeds;
   - weights: queen vs second-order queen vs distance band (from Phase 2).
5. **Detection power on a known signal.** Plant synthetic signals in null
   surfaces simulated from the Phase 6 base model, which keeps the observed
   zero structure and autocorrelation:
   - a 2-km "avoidance halo" (–50% inside the leases);
   - a "spillover ring" (+50% at 2–4 km).
   Measure sensitivity and false-positive rate for each statistic after FDR.
   This is the most direct measure of efficacy for *this* question.
6. **Stage-change readability.** Do the change classes (`gained hot`,
   `lost hot`, …) from each method line up with the BAG estimates from Phase 5?
   Agreement with the model is the external validation.

### Steps

1. Run `localmoran_perm(nsim = 999, iseed = 42)` and
   `localG_perm(nsim = 999, iseed = 42)` on `y_vst` for each dataset × gear ×
   stage. Apply BH-FDR within each surface at q = 0.05 and q = 0.10.
2. Build classes:
   - Gi\* bins −3…+3 (99/95/90%), as in the archive;
   - LISA quadrants, using `hotspot()` with `p.adjust = "fdr"`.
3. Stage-change classes S1→S2, S2→S3 and S1→S3. Keep the archived mutually
   exclusive scheme so results compare with the poster, and report the
   area (km²) in each class by `dist_band`.
4. Score criteria 1–6 and write a comparison table.
5. Decide the primary method.

```{r}
#| label: phase3-local
lisa <- localmoran_perm(y, lw_W, nsim = 999, iseed = 42, alternative = "two.sided")
gi   <- localG_perm(y, lw_B_self, nsim = 999, iseed = 42, alternative = "two.sided")
lisa_class <- hotspot(lisa, Prname = "Pr(z != E(Ii)) Sim", cutoff = 0.05,
                      p.adjust = "fdr")
gi_class   <- hotspot(gi, Prname = "Pr(z != E(Gi)) Sim", cutoff = 0.05,
                      p.adjust = "fdr")
```

**Expected outcome, to be confirmed by the criteria.**

- **Gi\* is primary** for hotspot mapping and stage-change classes: it is
  stable on sparse surfaces and reads directly as "where is effort
  concentrated".
- **LISA is secondary**, for its HL/LH outliers inside and next to the leases,
  which is where turbine-associated fixed-gear activity would show.
- LL and Gi\* cold results on AFE are reported as uninformative by
  construction.

**Gate.** If the criterion-5 power for a 2-km halo is below about 0.5 for both
statistics, say that the hotspot maps are descriptive and that inference about
project effects rests on the BAG models.

**Optional extension.** Emerging hot spot analysis on the monthly cubes
(`sfdep::emerging_hotspot_analysis`, a new dependency), for **mobile VP only**.
It is the only surface with enough temporal completeness (median 8 active
months per cell, 1,224 cells active in 12 or more months).

## Phase 4: Autocorrelated kernel density estimation, assessed and dropped {#sec-akde}

**Decision (interview, 2026-10-18): drop AKDE.** The assessment that supports
the decision:

- **What AKDE needs.** AKDE (Fleming et al. 2015; `ctmm`) estimates an
  individual's utilisation distribution from *timestamped relocations*. It
  fits a continuous-time movement model to the empirical variogram of those
  fixes, then corrects the kernel bandwidth for autocorrelation. It needs:
  - irregular or regular fixes with times, per individual;
  - enough fixes to resolve the home-range crossing time;
  - range residency (a stationary home range).
- **What these data are.** The 4Wings extract is vessel × 0.01° cell ×
  *day* aggregates. It has no within-day timestamps, no positions finer than
  the cell, and an unknown number of fixes behind each "1 h". Building
  pseudo-fixes from cell centroids and dates would:
  - impose a 1-day time step and an approximately 1 km spatial quantum,
    making the variogram an artefact of the aggregation;
  - violate range residency for transiting and multi-port vessels;
  - answer a different question (*individual vessel ranges*) from the one in
    this plan (*where effort is, by cell, and how it changes*).
- **Value against cost.** AKDE would add no inferential value over the
  cell-level models and would add a methodological weakness reviewers would
  pick up. It would be valid only with point-level AIS, for example
  MarineCadastre 1-minute AIS for selected vessels, and that is out of scope.
- **What replaces it for visualisation.**
  1. Model-based smoothed density surfaces: the predicted mean from the
     Phase 6 or 7 spatial-field models, with uncertainty.
  2. **Posterior exceedance-probability maps** from INLA,
     P(density > baseline 90th percentile), as a model-based hotspot surface
     that connects Phases 3 and 7.
  3. For display only, a fixed-bandwidth kernel smooth of cell-centroid
     densities with `KernSmooth::bkde2D` (already in `renv.lock`). Label it
     as smoothing, not estimation.

## Phase 5: Infrastructure data and BAG models (`09_infrastructure.qmd`, `10_bag.qmd`) {#sec-bag}

### Ørsted turbine and cable data: specification {#sec-infra}

Ask Ørsted for, or build, a table with the schema below. Store it under
`data/sf/infra/` (GeoPackage, EPSG:32619). Document it in
`references/data_dictionary.md`, and note in `references/` where it came
from and what terms it was shared under.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `asset_id` | string | Unique, stable |
| `project` | SFW / RWF / SRW | |
| `asset_type` | `wtg` (turbine), `oss` (substation), `iac` (inter-array cable), `export_cable` | |
| `geometry` | POINT (WTG, OSS) / LINESTRING (cables) | |
| `foundation_installed`, `wtg_installed`, `first_power` | date | Turbines and substations |
| `lay_start`, `lay_end`, `burial_complete` | date | Cables |
| `source`, `version_date` | string / date | Provenance |

Derived covariates per cell × month (in `09`):

- `d_wtg_km(t)`: distance to the nearest turbine *foundation installed by
  month t* (`Inf` before the first one);
- `n_wtg_2km(t)`: installed turbines within 2 km;
- `d_cable_km(t)`: distance to the nearest laid cable;
- `active_construction(t)`: the cell is within *r* km of an asset installed
  that month;
- `months_since_first_wtg`: per project, for event-time plots.

Tests check that every date falls inside the analysis window or is blank, that
the geometry is valid and in the AOI, and that distances never increase as
more assets are installed.

### BAG design

Before–After–Gradient (Methratta 2020, 2021) estimates the change in the
**spatial gradient** of effort with distance from the development, between
the period before and the period after. Within-AOI changes that are uniform in
space cancel out of the gradient contrast.

**Cell × stage × gear** (per gear, per dataset):

$$
\log \mu_{c,s} = \beta_0 + \beta_s + f(d_c) + \gamma_s \, f(d_c) + \mathbf{z}_c^\top \boldsymbol{\delta} + \omega_c + \log(\text{months}_s \cdot \text{area}_c)
$$

- *d*<sub>c</sub> is `dist_band`, with 8–15 km as the reference, or a
  low-rank smooth of `dist_lease_km`.
- **z**<sub>c</sub> holds the static environmental covariates (@sec-env):
  `s(depth_m)`, slope, BPI and, once available, habitat shares.
- *γ*<sub>s</sub> are the **BAG effects**. The change in the inside / 0–2 km
  rate ratio between Stage 1 and Stages 2 and 3 is the headline estimate.
- *ω*<sub>c</sub> is a spatial random effect (Phase 6 decides its form).

**Cell × month × gear:** stages are replaced by time-varying exposure:

$$
\log \mu_{c,t} = \beta_0 + s_{\text{cc}}(\text{moy}_t) + s(\text{year}_t) + h\big(d^{\text{wtg}}_{c}(t)\big) + \text{phase}_{p(c),t} \times g(d_c) + \mathbf{z}_c^\top \boldsymbol{\delta} + \omega_c + \varepsilon_{c,t} + \log(\text{area}_c)
$$

- phase<sub>p,t</sub> ∈ {pre, construction, operation} comes from each cell's
  nearest project's Ørsted dates. The three projects run on different
  schedules, which gives a **staggered design**: cells near a project that has
  not started act as concurrent controls for cells near one that has.
- *h*(·) is the turbine-distance response, fitted only after the first
  installation.
- *ε*<sub>c,t</sub> is temporal correlation within a cell (AR1 on month or
  year; Phase 6).

**Steps**

1. Descriptive BAG: the rate by `dist_band` × stage (season-standardised),
   with bootstrap CIs over cells. Plot the gradient profile per stage per gear.
2. Event-time plot: monthly rate by band around each project's
   `first foundation` date (−24 to +24 months).
3. Fit the stage-level BAG for each gear × dataset with the family from
   @sec-treatments (NB2 for VP; Tweedie and delta-Gamma for AFE).
4. Fit the monthly BAG with the Ørsted covariates (needs `09`).
5. Formal gear contrast: a joint MOBILE + FIXED model with a `gear × period ×
   band` interaction, to test whether mobile and fixed gear respond
   differently.
6. Report the BAG rate ratios (exp *γ*) with 95% CI, marginal predicted
   densities by band × period, and the turbine-distance curve *h*(·).

### Limits of the within-AOI BAG {#sec-bag-limits}

- **The reference ring may itself be affected.** If displaced effort moves
  outward, the 8–15 km ring *gains* effort. The contrast then mixes near-field
  avoidance with far-field displacement, which exaggerates the gradient change.
  Read *γ* as **redistribution**, not net loss. A check: fit a continuous
  distance smooth and see whether the 8–15 km level departs from the Stage 1
  level.
- **The reference ring is small.** 130 cells are 10–15 km away, and the 8–15
  ring has 574. The gradient is short against the likely scale of displacement.
- **An AOI-wide change cannot be identified.** The stage main effects
  *β*<sub>s</sub> mix project effects with regional trends, COVID and AIS
  uptake. Report them, but do not interpret them as project effects.
- **Pre-trend check.** The parallel-trends test in Phase 1, step 7 must pass,
  or a pre-trend term is added (gate in @sec-phase1).

## Phase 6: Statistical models, comparison of approaches (`11_models_frequentist.qmd`, `12_models_inla.qmd`) {#sec-models}

### The three candidate approaches

| | **Tweedie GLMM** | **Hurdle (delta) model** | **Bayesian INLA-SPDE** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model | One compound Poisson–gamma likelihood, *Y* ~ Tw(*μ*, *φ*, *p*), log link | Two parts: Pr(*Y* > 0) by binomial (logit or cloglog); *Y* given *Y* > 0 by Gamma / lognormal (AFE) or truncated NB (VP) | Latent Gaussian model: any of the above likelihoods + a Matérn Gaussian random field approximated by an SPDE on a triangulated mesh, with approximate Bayesian inference (Laplace) |
| How zeros arise | From the same process as positive values (Poisson number of "events" = 0) | From a **separate** process with its own covariates | Set by the chosen likelihood (Tweedie, zero-inflated, or a joint two-likelihood hurdle) |
| Linear predictors | 1 | 2 (each with its own covariates and random effects) | 1 or 2 |
| Covariate effects | One effect on the mean | Separate effects on *whether* a cell is used and on *how much* | Full posteriors, including derived quantities (exceedance probabilities, rate-ratio posteriors) |
| Spatial dependence | `glmmTMB`: a cell random effect plus a spatial covariance (`exp()` / `mat()`), dense and slow for more than about 3k locations; or **`sdmTMB`**: an SPDE field (sparse, fast) | Same tools (`glmmTMB`, `sdmTMB` delta families), with a field in each part, shared or separate | SPDE Matérn field; spatiotemporal with `group` + AR1. No barrier needed: the AOI is open water. |
| Software | `glmmTMB` (`tweedie()`), `sdmTMB` (`tweedie()`), `mgcv` (`tw()`) | `glmmTMB` (`ziformula` / `truncated_nbinom2`), `sdmTMB` (`delta_gamma()`, `delta_lognormal()`, `delta_truncated_nbinom2()`) | `INLA` + `fmesher` (+ `inlabru`) |
| Speed (cell × stage, ≈10k rows) | Seconds to minutes | Minutes | Minutes |
| Speed (cell × month, ≈432k rows per gear) | Minutes (`sdmTMB` with an SPDE field) | Minutes to an hour | Hours. Needs a smaller domain or a coarser time step, or both. |
| Diagnostics | DHARMa (uniformity, dispersion, zero inflation), spatial Moran's I on residuals, *p* profile | DHARMa per part and combined, calibration of the binomial part | PIT / CPO, posterior predictive checks, prior-sensitivity refits, WAIC / DIC |
| Model comparison | AIC (same response), spatial-block CV (`sdmTMB_cv`) | AIC against Tweedie (same continuous response), block CV | WAIC, LCPO, `inla.group.cv` |

### What each approach requires

#### Tweedie GLMM: conditions

1. **Response:** continuous, non-negative, with exact zeros. Valid for AFE.
   For VP, a count family is more natural; Tweedie with *p* near 1 is only an
   approximation.
2. **1 < *p* < 2**, estimated rather than fixed. The power slopes measured so
   far (AFE about 1.7) satisfy this.
3. **One process.** The covariates must move *occupancy and intensity in the
   same direction*. The Tweedie mean folds both into one linear predictor,
   so if turbines cut the number of fishing cells but raise the intensity
   inside the ones still used (plausible for fixed gear), a Tweedie model
   averages the two and can show *no effect*.
4. **Zero frequency consistent with the mean.** Under Tweedie,
   Pr(0) = exp(−*μ*^(2−*p*) / (*φ*(2−*p*))). DHARMa's zero-inflation test
   must pass. At 97–99.7% zeros (monthly AFE) it often fails unless the
   domain is restricted.
5. **Residual independence after the random effects:** no residual spatial
   or temporal autocorrelation (DHARMa `testSpatialAutocorrelation`,
   `testTemporalAutocorrelation`).
6. Enough non-zero observations per estimated parameter, roughly 10 or more.

#### Hurdle (delta) model: conditions

1. **Zeros are a separate process, in substance.** Here that means a cell is
   *used or not* by a gear (avoidance, exclusion, access), and *intensity
   given use* is driven by other things. This is the most defensible
   interpretation near turbines and cables.
2. **Enough positive observations for the positive part**, per gear × time
   step. That holds for mobile at any scale and for fixed at the stage level.
   Fixed monthly AFE has only about 3,400 positive cell-months, which is
   enough for a parsimonious positive model if the domain is restricted. It
   does not hold for pole-and-line AFE (not modelled).
3. **Distribution of the positive part:**
   - AFE: Gamma (constant CV) or lognormal; choose by DHARMa and the
     mean–variance check.
   - VP: zero-truncated NB2.
4. **Correlation between the parts.** The two parts are fitted as
   independent unless they share a random field. `sdmTMB` delta models allow
   a shared or separate field per part. If a cell is attractive in both
   respects, ignoring that understates uncertainty in the combined
   prediction.
5. **Combining the parts for headline effects.** The marginal mean is
   Pr(*Y* > 0) × E[*Y* | *Y* > 0], so BAG effects for the mean must be
   *derived* (`marginaleffects`, or simulation), not read off one
   coefficient.
6. Residual checks on both parts, as for Tweedie.

#### Bayesian INLA-SPDE: conditions

1. **Latent Gaussian structure.** The linear predictor must be Gaussian given
   the hyperparameters, which holds for GLMM-type models with Gaussian random
   effects and fields. Supported likelihoods include `nbinomial`, `tweedie`,
   `gamma`, `binomial` and zero-inflated variants. A hurdle is a joint model
   of two likelihoods with a `copy` or shared field.
2. **Matérn field: stationary and isotropic.** Fishing grounds follow depth
   and substrate gradients, and the leases form sharp edges, so stationarity
   is an approximation. Fixed covariates absorb the non-stationary part:
   distance to the lease, bathymetry (@sec-env) and habitat when it arrives.
   - **The AOI does not touch land** (confirmed 2026-10-18), so the standard
     stationary SPDE applies and no barrier model (Bakka et al. 2019) is
     needed.
   - Check stationarity after the covariates by comparing range estimates
     from separate fits to the northern (RWF) and southern (SRW) halves of
     the AOI. A ratio above 2 would argue for a non-stationary extension.
   - **Spatial confounding.** A spatial field can soak up variation that a
     spatially smooth covariate like depth would otherwise explain, which
     shifts or widens its estimate. Compare the depth coefficients with and
     without the field. If they differ materially, report the field-free
     estimate as the covariate's descriptive association and rely on the
     BAG interaction for inference.
3. **Mesh design.**
   - Maximum inner edge ≤ *ρ*₀ / 5, with *ρ*₀ the practical range from the
     Phase 2 correlogram.
   - Cutoff about 1 km, the cell size.
   - Outer extension of at least *ρ*₀ to avoid boundary effects.
   - Check that results do not change between two mesh resolutions.
4. **Priors.** Penalised-complexity priors on range and SD (Fuglstad et al.
   2019), e.g. P(*ρ* < *ρ*₀/2) = 0.05 and P(*σ* > 1) = 0.05, plus a
   **prior-sensitivity refit** that doubles and halves *ρ*₀.
5. **Laplace approximation accuracy.** It can be poor for very sparse binary
   data (the occupancy part of a monthly fixed hurdle). Check against
   `control.inla = list(strategy = "laplace")` and posterior predictive
   checks.
6. **Data support.** INLA treats each cell centroid as a point. For a regular
   lattice an **areal BYM2 model** (`f(cell, model = "bym2", graph = queen)`)
   is the natural alternative. Fit it as a sensitivity: it uses the same
   queen graph as Phases 2–3, while the SPDE handles the continuous-space
   turbine-distance covariates and prediction.
7. **Computing.** Cell × month with a spatiotemporal AR1 field over 128
   months is large. Fit on the gear domain, at season × year (about 43 time
   steps), or with a yearly AR1 field plus a fixed cyclic month term.
   Record wall time and memory.
8. **Reproducibility.** `INLA` is not on CRAN.
   - Set its repository in `renv` (`options(repos = c(INLA = ...))`) so the
     lockfile records the version.
   - Results can change slightly between INLA versions, so record
     `INLA::inla.version()` in the provenance sidecar.
   - Windows binaries need a matching R minor version, which is 4.5 here.

### Recommendation

A **tiered strategy**, chosen by data shape rather than by habit:

1. **Primary inferential models: `sdmTMB`** with an SPDE spatial field, plus
   a spatiotemporal field by stage (stage tables) or a yearly AR1 field
   (monthly tables). Families:
   - **VP: NB2.** Delta-truncated-NB2 if zero inflation is flagged.
   - **AFE: delta-Gamma.** Tweedie is fitted as the direct comparison.

   `sdmTMB` brings the SPDE machinery of INLA into a fast, frequentist,
   DHARMa-compatible framework. Its developers built it for fisheries survey
   and effort data of exactly this shape.
2. **Tweedie vs hurdle.** Decide per gear × dataset × time step by:
   - spatial-block cross-validation (`sdmTMB_cv`, block size ≥ *ρ*₀), using
     the out-of-fold log predictive density;
   - DHARMa diagnostics;
   - whether the hurdle's two parts give BAG effects with **opposite signs**.
     If so, the hurdle is required on substance, whatever the CV score.
3. **`glmmTMB`** without a spatial field (cell random effect only) as the
   simple, transparent baseline, to show what the spatial field changes.
4. **INLA-SPDE as the confirmatory Bayesian model** for the headline BAG
   results, for the mobile and fixed stage-level models and the mobile
   monthly model. It adds:
   - full posteriors for the BAG rate ratios;
   - **exceedance-probability maps** that replace AKDE visually (@sec-akde);
   - a check that the frequentist conclusions survive a different inferential
     framework and the prior-sensitivity refits.

### Model specifications (sketch)

```{r}
#| label: phase6-sdmtmb
library(sdmTMB)
d    <- afe_stage |> filter(gear_class == "MOBILE")
mesh <- make_mesh(d, c("x_km", "y_km"), cutoff = 1)   # refine from rho0 (Phase 2)

m_tw <- sdmTMB(afe_hours ~ 0 + stage * dist_band + s(depth_m, k = 4) + slope_z + bpi_z,
               data = d, mesh = mesh, family = tweedie(link = "log"),
               offset = d$log_expo,
               spatial = "on", spatiotemporal = "iid", time = "stage_num")

m_dg <- update(m_tw, family = delta_gamma())          # hurdle

# VP monthly, mobile
m_vp <- sdmTMB(vp_hours ~ 0 + phase * dist_band + s(moy, bs = "cc", k = 8) + s(year, k = 5) +
                 s(depth_m, k = 4) + slope_z + bpi_z,
               data = vp_month_mobile, mesh = mesh_m, family = nbinom2(),
               offset = vp_month_mobile$log_expo,
               spatial = "on", spatiotemporal = "ar1", time = "year",
               knots = list(moy = c(0.5, 12.5)))

cv_tw <- sdmTMB_cv(..., fold_ids = spatial_block_folds(d, size_km = rho0), k_folds = 5)
```

```{r}
#| label: phase7-inla
library(INLA); library(fmesher)
mesh <- fm_mesh_2d(loc = cbind(d$x_km, d$y_km), max.edge = c(rho0 / 5, rho0),
                   cutoff = 1, offset = c(2, rho0))
spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(mesh, prior.range = c(rho0 / 2, 0.05),
                            prior.sigma = c(1, 0.05))
idx  <- inla.spde.make.index("w", n.spde = spde$n.spde, n.group = 3)
A    <- inla.spde.make.A(mesh, loc = cbind(d$x_km, d$y_km),
                         group = d$stage_num, n.group = 3)
stk  <- inla.stack(data = list(y = d$afe_hours, E = exp(d$log_expo)),
                   A = list(A, 1), effects = list(idx, d[, c("stage", "dist_band")]))
fit  <- inla(y ~ 0 + stage * dist_band +
               f(w, model = spde, group = w.group, control.group = list(model = "ar1")),
             family = "tweedie", data = inla.stack.data(stk), E = E,
             control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stk), compute = TRUE),
             control.compute = list(waic = TRUE, cpo = TRUE, config = TRUE))
```

### Vessel-level extension (optional) {#sec-models-vessel}

To deal directly with vessel concentration (caveat 12), aggregate the
record-level Primary data to **cell × stage × MMSI**, with zeros for vessels
active in the gear that stage. Fit the BAG with an `(1 | MMSI)` random
effect, or a random slope on distance by vessel. This splits *fleet-wide
redistribution* from *a few vessels moving*. It is costly in rows and is
optional; the leave-one-vessel-out jackknife (Phase 8) is the minimum.

**Gate for Phases 6–7.**

- Residual Moran's I is not significant at q = 0.05.
- DHARMa uniformity and dispersion pass, or any failures are explained.
- Mesh and prior sensitivity change the BAG rate ratios by less than 10%.
- Adding the environmental covariates changes the BAG rate ratios by less than
  10%. They are static, so they should not; a larger change means distance
  and habitat are entangled, and is reported.
- Tweedie and hurdle agree in sign on the marginal BAG effect, or the
  disagreement is reported as a finding.

## Phase 8: Sensitivity (`13_sensitivity.qmd`) {#sec-sensitivity}

Run the headline Gi\* change classes, the stage-level BAG rate ratios and the
monthly BAG turbine-distance curve on each variant. Report the results as a
grid: variant × outcome, with the estimate and CI.

| Variant | Purpose |
|---|---|
| Strict vs Primary (all-gear) | The effect of vessel processing, as a result in its own right |
| Drop `edge` + `outside` cells | AOI boundary effects |
| Drop dual-permitted MMSIs (`vessel_permit_groups.csv`) | Gear assignment for mixed-fishery vessels |
| AFE with imputed effort for added hulls (from `04`) | The undercount in caveat 3 |
| Drop AFE records < 0.32 h | Continuity with the archived threshold |
| Leave out each of the top 10 MMSIs per gear | Vessel concentration |
| Restore PROVIDER's 2020-06-18 → 2020-09-30 hours to Stage 1 | Effect of the caveat 11 decision on the baseline |
| Exclude 2020 | COVID, and the Stage 1/2 boundary |
| With / without environmental covariates (bathymetry; habitat once available) | Stability of the BAG effects (@sec-env) |
| Ørsted habitat vs regional substrate (if Ørsted coverage is partial) | Habitat source |
| Raw vs season-standardised stage rates | Caveat 8 |
| Alternative transform (√ ↔ log) and weights (queen / 2-order / distance band) | Phase 3 robustness |
| Fleet-size covariate (active MMSIs per gear per month) | AIS uptake |
| Distance bands vs a continuous distance smooth | BAG specification |

## Phase 9: Synthesis (`14_synthesis.qmd`) {#sec-synthesis}

- **Headline results:**
  - BAG rate ratios by gear × dataset, from `sdmTMB` with INLA alongside;
  - turbine-distance response curves;
  - Gi\* change maps by gear, with LISA outliers overlaid inside the leases.
- **Methods contribution:**
  - Strict vs Primary;
  - the season-composition confound;
  - the LISA-vs-Gi\* comparison and its power simulation;
  - why AKDE was dropped.
- **Limitations section** built from @sec-caveats, every number computed at
  render time.
- **Figures** as PNG + vector PDF, on the archived poster palette and basemap
  for visual continuity.

## FAIR implementation {#sec-fair}

| Principle | Practice in this workflow |
|---|---|
| **Findable** | Tagged releases with a Zenodo DOI. `CITATION.cff` updated for the R methods: its abstract still describes the archived geopandas/esda workflow. Every derived file listed in `references/data_dictionary.md` with keywords. Stable, descriptive file names (`{dataset}_{timestep}_gear.csv`). |
| **Accessible** | Code under MIT. Derived GFW products (cell tables, model outputs) released under **CC BY-SA 4.0**, as GFW's share-alike licence requires, with attribution. GARFO-derived fields are never released beyond the permit group, as in `03`. Raw GFW extracts can be regenerated with the documented `gfwr` calls; the 2026-10-06 pull is archived as a dated deposit so the vessel decisions stay reproducible. |
| **Interoperable** | GeoPackage with the CRS declared (EPSG:32619), and CSV in UTF-8 with ISO 8601 dates. Units in column names (`_hours`, `_km`, `_km2`). Controlled vocabularies for `gear_class`, `stage`, `dist_band` and `asset_type`, documented in the data dictionary. Spatial weights as a GAL file. An optional Frictionless `datapackage.json` (written with `jsonlite`, no new dependency) describing each table's schema. |
| **Reusable** | `renv.lock` pins every package, including INLA's repository. Every qmd is parameterised (`set`, `gear`, `dataset`, path overrides) in the existing `paths.R` pattern. Seeds are fixed (`set.seed(42)`, `iseed = 42`). A **provenance sidecar** (`<file>.json`) for every output: input file hashes (`digest`), the GFW `pull_date`, the git commit (`gert`), the renv lockfile hash, R and INLA versions, and the seed. `testthat` tests for every new helper. `sessionInfo()` and `renv::diagnostics()` at the end of every render. No typed statistics in prose. |

```{r}
#| label: fair-sidecar
write_provenance <- function(out_path, inputs, extra = list()) {
  meta <- c(list(
    file = basename(out_path), written = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE),
    inputs = lapply(setNames(inputs, basename(inputs)), \(f) digest::digest(file = f, algo = "sha256")),
    git_commit = gert::git_info()$commit,
    renv_lock_sha256 = digest::digest(file = "renv.lock", algo = "sha256"),
    r_version = R.version.string, seed = 42L), extra)
  jsonlite::write_json(meta, paste0(out_path, ".json"), auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE)
}
```

## Timeline (about 20 weeks) {#sec-timeline}

| Weeks | Phase | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0: Analysis tables, weights, bathymetry covariates, helpers, tests | — |
| 2–3 | 1: EDA (gate: parallel trends, PROVIDER) | 0 |
| 3–4 | 2: Global statistics, correlograms (*ρ*₀) | 0 |
| 4–6 | 3: Local Moran's I vs Gi\* (needs the base model from 6 for the power simulation; run criteria 1–4 first and 5 later) | 2 |
| — | 4: AKDE, done here (dropped) | — |
| 5–7 | 5a: Ørsted infrastructure ingest and covariates | Ørsted data |
| When received | Ørsted habitat ingest: coverage check, per-cell shares, refit the affected models | Ørsted habitat |
| 6–9 | 5b: Stage-level BAG (no Ørsted data needed), then monthly BAG | 1, 5a |
| 8–12 | 6: `sdmTMB` / `glmmTMB` Tweedie vs hurdle, CV, diagnostics | 2, 5 |
| 12–16 | 7: INLA-SPDE confirmatory, BYM2 sensitivity | 6 |
| 16–18 | 8: Sensitivity grid | 3, 6 |
| 18–20 | 9: Synthesis, FAIR release, DOI | all |

The stage-level BAG and all of Phases 1–3 can go ahead before the Ørsted data
arrive. Only the monthly BAG (5b, second half) and the turbine-distance
covariates wait for them.
